papers.title_in_file: Observation of Quantum Zeno Blockade on Chip
papers.version_note: arXiv:1703.09830v2 (10 Apr 2017). The text matches the record.
papers.what_it_is: An experimental paper reporting quantum Zeno blockade (interaction-free all-optical modulation) in an air-suspended lithium niobate on insulator microdisk, with bright pulses and with attenuated single-photon-level pulses.

assertions.value: The authors describe the quantum Zeno effect as occurring when a coherently evolving quantum system is strongly coupled to external degrees of freedom (an environment or reservoir), with the result that the evolution is suppressed or frozen.
quotes: The quantum Zeno effect occurs when a coherently evolving quantum system is strongly
coupled to external degrees of freedom, often referred to as “environment” or a reservoir, with the result that the evolution is suppressed or frozen
assertions.certainty_reason: Background description attributed by the authors to earlier work, not a result of this paper.

assertions.value: The authors define quantum Zeno blockade (QZB) as occurring when a photonic system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear-optical channel, so that, when the nonlinear coupling is strong, occupation of a certain mode by a single photon can block (more precisely, suppress) additional photons from coupling into the system.
quotes: QZB occurs when a photonic system interacts with external degrees of freedom through a nonlinear-optical channel
occupation of a certain mode of the system by a single photon can “block” (more precisely, suppress) additional photons from coupling into the system
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines the term it uses in the introduction.

assertions.value: The authors state that the nonlinear interaction in QZB acts as a continuous probe monitoring the photon occupation of the system, and that the interaction can be dissipative (such as two-photon absorption) or coherent (such as sum or difference frequency generation).
quotes: the nonlinear interaction functions as a continuous probe “monitoring” the system’s photon occupation
The interaction can be dissipative, like that of two-photon absorption
or be coherent such as sum or difference frequency generation
assertions.certainty_reason: An author statement of mechanism, with citations to the authors' earlier theory work, not tested in this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: This experiment uses the coherent route (sum frequency generation).

assertions.value: The authors state that, unlike photon blockade mediated by single atoms, no excitation (excited atoms, excitons or equivalents) is physically created for the blockade to take effect, and that this interaction-free and excitation-free feature eliminates phase noise, dissipation and decoherence.
quotes: here no excitation, either excited atoms, excitons or their equivalences, is physically created in order for the blockade to take effect
This distinct interaction-free and excitation-free features combined eliminate the phase noise, dissipation, and decoherence (such as via spontaneous emission)
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors support this with citations to their earlier analyses; the present experiment does not measure decoherence.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper reports no measurement of phase noise or decoherence; its noise measurement concerns spontaneous Raman and parametric photons only.

assertions.value: The authors state that, to date, all demonstrations of quantum Zeno effects have used bulk optical systems, which they describe as not suitable for scaling.
quotes: to date all demonstrations of quantum Zeno effects have used bulk optical systems, which are not suitable for scaling
assertions.certainty_reason: A statement about prior work that the paper attributes to cited work.
assertions.reader_inference: The paper states this for the quantum Zeno effect in general, not only for QZB.

assertions.value: The authors state that they have found, for a low-loss nonlinear microcavity, that QZB allows deterministic interaction between single photons, which may enable scalable photonic quantum computing without post selection or auxiliary photons.
quotes: implemented in a low-loss nonlinear microcavity, QZB allows deterministic interaction between single photons
which may enable scalable photonic quantum computing, i.e., without post selection nor use of auxiliary photons
assertions.certainty_reason: A result the authors attribute to their earlier theory work; this paper does not demonstrate photon-photon interaction.
assertions.reader_inference: The present experiment modulates single-photon-level pulses with a bright pump; it does not show interaction between two single photons.

assertions.value: The authors use an air-suspended microdisk cavity nanofabricated on a z-cut lithium niobate on insulator (LNOI) film, with a 500-nm thick film etched down to 200 nm and a microdisk radius of around 20 µm.
quotes: an air-suspended microdisk cavity nanofabricated on a z-cut LNOI
we start with a 500-nm thick LNOI thin ﬁlm and etch it down to only 200 nm
we choose the microdisk radius to be around 20 µm
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own device geometry in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use quasi-TE modes for the telecom light waves and quasi-TM modes for the near-IR wave, together with the geometric dispersion of the confined whispering-gallery modes, and that this achieves phase matching for second-harmonic generation between light waves near 1550 nm and 775 nm in the fundamental spatial modes.
quotes: we use quasi-transverse-electric (quasi-TE) modes for the telecom light waves and quasi-transverse-magnetic (quasi-TM) modes for the near-IR wave
phase matching for the secondharmonic generation between light waves near 1550 nm and 775 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their phase-matching design in Section 1.
assertions.reader_inference: The text cites finite element simulation for the mode profiles and says the experiment verified it.

assertions.value: The authors state that, for the z-cut crystal orientation, the second-order processes go through the d31 and d32 tensor elements, which are 4 to 5 times lower than the largest element d33 of lithium niobate, and that they expect to overcome this with periodic poling in future work.
quotes: the χ(2) processes are through the d31 and d32 tensor elements, which are 4 to 5 times lower than the largest element d33 of lithium niobate
We expect to overcome this deﬁciency by applying centric periodic poling
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of their current device in Section 1.

assertions.value: The authors report a free spectral range between fundamental whispering-gallery modes of 9.1 nm near 1546 nm for a microdisk, and a smallest cavity linewidth of about 0.06 nm, which corresponds to a loaded cavity quality factor of 2.6 × 104 (the exponent is printed flat in the text layer; read as ten to the fourth).
quotes: the free spectral range (FSR) between the fundamental WGM’s is measured to be 9.1 nm near 1546 nm
The smallest cavity linewidth is about 0.06 nm, which corresponds to a loaded cavity quality factor of 2.6 × 104
assertions.certainty_reason: A measured value from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The 0.06 nm linewidth is the smallest found; the paper reports no Q for the specific modes used in the QZB runs.

assertions.value: The authors state that the tapered fiber used as the evanescent coupler has a transmission loss as low as 0.05 dB upon tapering, increasing to around 1 dB after extended exposure in ambient air, and that coupling efficiency to the microdisk is sensitive to relative position.
quotes: Its transmission loss can be as low as 0.05 dB upon tapering, but increases to around 1 dB after extended exposure in ambient air.
The coupling efﬁciency of the
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state a property of their own coupling setup.

assertions.value: The authors report that, with a continuous-wave pump of milliwatt level coupled into a fundamental quasi-TE mode around 1546 nm, they observe generated second-harmonic light around 773 nm with a clear quadratic dependence on input pump power, which they take to verify the frequency doubling process.
quotes: a miliwatt continuous-wave (CW) pump light into a fundamental quasi-TE mode around 1546 nm
The generated second-harmonic light (around 773 nm)
a clear quadratic dependency is seen, thus verifying the frequency doubling process
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device; the figure itself is not quoted.
assertions.reader_inference: The text gives 775 nm as the design wavelength and 773 nm for the observed second harmonic; the paper does not comment on the difference.

assertions.value: The authors report that the strongest sum-frequency generation occurs between two adjacent fundamental quasi-TE modes at 1536.790 nm and 1545.900 nm, and that for continuous-wave light the cavity resonances can thermally drift by as much as 0.1 nm, which exceeds their linewidth.
quotes: the strongest SFG occurs between two adjacent fundamental quasi-TE modes, each at 1536.790 nm and 1545.900 nm
the cavity resonances can thermally drift by as high as 0.1 nm, which exceeds their linewidth
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation from one device.

assertions.value: The authors describe three synchronized optical channels: a pump pulse train of 1 MHz repetition rate and 250 ps FWHM; a quasi-continuous-wave signal with 1-MHz repetition rate and 10-ns FWHM; and signal pulses at a 50 MHz repetition rate and 200 ps FWHM.
quotes: Channel 1 creates a pump pulse train of 1 MHz repetition rate and 250 ps FWHM.
Channel 2 produces a quasi-CW signal with 1-MHz repetition rate and 10-ns FWHM.
Channel 3 generates signal pulses at a 50 MHz repetition rate and 200 ps FWHM.
assertions.certainty_reason: The Fig. 4 caption states the authors' own experimental setup.

assertions.value: The authors state that the average (peak) power coupled into the microdisk is approximately 170 µW (680 mW) for the pump, and 4 µw (400 µW) for the signal, and that pump and signal wavelengths were fine tuned by less than 0.05 nm to hit slightly drifted resonance centers.
quotes: The average (peak) power coupled into the microdisk is approximately 170 µW (680 mW) for the pump, and 4 µw (400 µW) for the signal.
we ﬁne tune the wavelengths of the pump and signal by less than 0.05 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own operating powers.
assertions.reader_inference: The text earlier gives about 250 µW as the low average power target for limiting thermal effects; the 170 µW pump average is the coupled figure and the text does not reconcile the two.

assertions.value: The authors define the modulation extinction as the ratio between the QZB-induced reduction in the transmission loss and the loss when the signal is at the cavity-resonance center without QZB.
quotes: deﬁned as the ratio between the QZB-induced reduction in the transmission loss to the loss when the signal is at the cavity-resonance center without QZB
assertions.certainty_reason: The paper defines its own figure of merit.
assertions.reader_inference: The pulsed results are consistent with this definition: the reduction 32.8 percent minus 14.4 percent divided by the 38.1 percent resonance-center loss is about 48 percent.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest modulation extinction of 51.0% for a quasi-continuous-wave signal with a pulsed pump, obtained when the signal is blue detuned from its resonance center by 0.01 nm, and an extinction ratio of 16.3% or less for further blue detuning.
quotes: is 51.0%, obtained when the signal is blue detuned from its resonance center by 0.01 nm
Further blue detuning the signal reduces the extinction ratio to 16.3% or less.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: This is the largest extinction reported in the paper; the single-photon-level result is 20.6 percent, with a pump and signal pair the authors say is less well phase matched.

assertions.value: The authors report that when the signal is red detuned its depletion through the disk is enhanced by the pump, and they state that these results show the pump-driven sum-frequency generation effectively alters the signal's cavity resonance while shifting it to a shorter wavelength, similar to the ac Stark shift for a two-level atom.
quotes: when the signal is red detuned, its depletion through the disk is enhanced by the pump
the SFG driven by the pump effectively alters the signal’s cavity resonance while shifting it to a shorter wavelength
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical observation with the authors' interpretation.
assertions.reader_inference: The shift interpretation is the authors' reading of the detuning dependence; the paper does not report a separate measurement of the shifted resonance.

assertions.value: The authors state that, in contrast to the thermally induced resonance drift that affects all cavity lines, the resonance altering applies to only a single resonant line satisfying the phase matching condition for sum-frequency generation.
quotes: In contrast to the thermally-induced resonance drift that affects all cavity lines, here the resonance altering applies to only a single resonant line satisfying the phase matching condition for SFG.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author claim; the text does not describe a measurement of other cavity lines.

assertions.value: The authors state that, according to their simulation, the shift of the optimal signal wavelength is likely due to imperfect phase mismatching, where the generated sum-frequency light is slightly off a resonance center.
quotes: According to our simulation, this shifted
optimal wavelength for the signal is likely due to the imperfect phase mismatching, where the generated SF light is slightly off a resonance center
assertions.certainty_reason: An author interpretation backed by an unreported simulation.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says 'imperfect phase mismatching'; read with the later text this likely means imperfect phase matching.

assertions.value: The authors state that they use different repetition rates for the pump (1 MHz) and signal pulses (50 MHz) to distinguish QZB from thermally induced effects, so that only one in fifty signal pulses overlaps a pump pulse, that overlapping peaks are coincident within 10 ps, and that a tunable optical delay moves pulses apart for the no-QZB reference, which in the pulsed-comparison figure is a displacement of 300 ps.
quotes: we use different pulse repetition rates for the pump (1 MHz) and signal pulses (50 MHz)
The pump and signal are temporally aligned so that the peaks of the overlapping pulses are coincident within 10 ps.
we later use a tunable optical delay to temporally misplace the pulses
completely displaced from the pump pulse by 300 ps
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own control design in Section 2.

assertions.value: The authors report that without pump overlap about 38.1% of the input signal power is lost in the microdisk at the resonance center, attributed to cavity under-coupling, and that with QZB the loss becomes 29.3%, which they state corresponds to a 23.0% reduction.
quotes: about 38.1% of the input signal power is lost in the microdisk at the resonance center, which is a result of the cavity under-coupling
at the resonance center, the signal loss with QZB becomes 29.3%, which corresponds to a 23.0% reduction
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The reduction (38.1 minus 29.3) divided by 38.1 is about 23 percent, consistent with the stated value.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the signal blue detuned by 0.01 nm its transmittance loss becomes 14.4% with the pump and 32.8% without the pump, giving a 48.2% modulation extinction caused by QZB.
quotes: when the signal is blue detuned by 0.01 nm, its transmittance loss becomes 14.4% with the pump and 32.8% without the pump, giving a 48.2% modulation extinction
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: Using the paper's definition, (32.8 minus 14.4) divided by the 38.1 percent resonance-center loss is about 48.3 percent, consistent with the stated 48.2 percent.

assertions.value: The authors report that with the signal further blue detuned to 0.02 nm the extinction drops to 40.0%, and they state that this variation of QZB effectiveness is because the sum-frequency generation is not perfectly phase matched in the current microdisk, in concord with their numerical simulation.
quotes: When the signal is further blue detuned to 0.02 nm, however, the extinction drops to 40.0%.
because the SFG is not perfectly phase matched in the current microdisk, as concord with our numerical simulation
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result with an author explanation from an unreported simulation.

assertions.value: The caption of the continuous-wave figure states that the resonant wavelength is 1536.790 nm for the pump and 1545.900 nm for the signal, while the caption of the pulsed-comparison figure states that the signal is blue detuned from the resonance center (1536.790 nm).
assertions.anchor: Fig. 5 caption p.11; Fig. 6 caption p.13
quotes: wavelength is 1536.790 nm for the pump and 1545.900 nm for the signal.
when they are blue detuned from the resonance center (1536.790 nm) by ∆λ = 0, 0.01, 0.02 nm
assertions.certainty_reason: The two captions are quoted as written; they differ on which wavelength belongs to the signal.
assertions.reader_inference: The two captions disagree on whether the 1536.790 nm mode carries the pump or the signal. The paper does not resolve this in the text read, so the assignment for the pulsed run is uncertain.

assertions.value: The authors state that, limited by their available filters, they select two non-adjacent fundamental quasi-TE modes for the pump and signal at 1545.900 nm and 1564.750 nm, and that this selection reduces the QZB efficiency by more than half because the sum-frequency generation becomes less phase matched.
quotes: we select two non-adjacent fundamental quasi-TE WGM’s for the pump and signal, at 1545.900 nm and 1564.750 nm, respectively
This wavelength selection unfortunately reduces the QZB efﬁciency by more than half as the SFG becomes less phase matched.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state this limit of their single-photon experiment in Section 3.

assertions.value: The authors state that the output uses two cascaded dense-wavelength-division multiplexers, each measured at 200-GHz FWHM bandwidth and around 50 dB extinction, and that photons are counted with a commercial InGaAs single-photon detector (ID210, ID Quantique) of 10.0% quantum efficiency, averaged over 2 million signal pulses.
quotes: Each DWDM ﬁlter is measured to have a 200-GHz FWHM bandwith and around 50 dB extinction.
The resulting photons are counted using a commercial InGaAs single-photon detector (ID210, ID Quantique) with a 10.0% quantum efﬁciency, and the measurement is averaged over 2 million signal pulses.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own detection setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The text says more than 100 dB of filtering extinction is required for the output signal photons; two filters at around 50 dB each give about that.

assertions.value: The authors derive the intrinsic noise level by comparing photon counts with and without the microdisk, using a per-length fiber noise rate Rf from fiber-only counts (fiber lengths of 3 m before and 4 m after the microdisk, a total detection efficiency of 8.6%) and then solving for the rate Rr of out-coupled noise photons created in the microdisk in the signal band.
quotes: L1 = 3 m and L2 = 4 m are the ﬁber lengths before and after the microdisk, respectively
η is the total detection efﬁciency, which is 8.6% for the current setup
calculate Rr, the rate of out-coupled noise photons created in the microdisk in the signal band
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own noise-derivation method and parameters.

assertions.value: The authors tabulate (Table 1) a gating rate of 939.4 (±0.1%) and a detection rate of 6.65 (±1.0%) without the disk, and a gating rate of 935.6 (±0.8%) and a detection rate of 7.12 (±1.0%) with the disk, in kHz, and attribute the difference in gating rates to the detector dead time of 10 µs.
quotes: the difference in the two detector gating rates is due to the detector dead time (10 µs)
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical measurement from one setup.

assertions.value: The authors report an out-coupled noise photon rate created in the microdisk in the signal band of Rr = 9.3 × 10−2 per pump pulse, for a pump pulse FWHM of 250 ps and a peak power of 680 mW (the exponent is printed flat in the text layer; read as ten to the minus two).
quotes: This gives Rr = 9.3 × 10−2 per pump pulse, for the current pump pulse FWHM of 250 ps and peak power of 680 mW.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result derived from one measurement set.
assertions.reader_inference: The result is derived from small differences between two counts (6.65 and 7.12 kHz, each with a stated uncertainty of 1.0 percent) and from fiber and coupling loss parameters, so its uncertainty is not stated in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors state that the DWDM filters together give a spectral bandwidth of 200 GHz (FWHM) with about 13 detected time-frequency modes, and that by pushing to single-mode detection the noise photon probability can be reduced to 7.2 × 10−3 per signal mode (the exponent is printed flat in the text layer; read as ten to the minus three), and to a negligible level by further detuning.
quotes: 200 GHz (FWHM), the number of detected time-frequency modes is about 13.
the noise photon probability can be reduced to 7.2 × 10−3 per signal mode
By further detuning the signal and pump, the noise level can be suppressed to negligible
assertions.certainty_reason: A projection derived from one measurement and an assumed single-mode detection.
assertions.reader_inference: The figure follows from dividing 9.3 × 10−2 by 13 (about 7.2 × 10−3); single-mode detection was not performed in this experiment.

assertions.value: The authors attribute the relatively low intrinsic noise level of the LNOI microdisk, even for the present small detuning between signal and pump, to its air suspended geometry, isolated phonon modes, and a relatively small Raman scattering cross-section.
quotes: The relatively low intrinsic noise level of the LNOI microdisk—even for the present small detuning between the signal and pump—is due to its air suspended geometry
isolated phonon modes
assertions.certainty_reason: An author explanation supported by citations; the paper does not test each cause separately.

assertions.value: The authors state that they expect that, for the pump and signal in the telecom C-band and with improved nanofabrication for a higher cavity Q, the level of noise photons can reach or exceed the dark count level of a typical InGaAs single-photon detector, about 10−5 per pulse (the exponent is printed flat in the text layer; read as ten to the minus five).
quotes: upon improved nanofabrication techniques for a higher cavity Q, the level of noise photon can reach or exceed the dark count level of a typical InGaAs single-photon detector
which is about 10−5 per pulse
assertions.certainty_reason: An author expectation, not a measured result.

assertions.value: The authors state that the single-photon-level demonstration uses attenuated laser pulses, each containing 0.16 photons on average, and that the results are given after subtracting the total detection background at 7.12 KHz, which includes detector dark counts and in-band noise photons created by the pump in the microdisk and fibers.
quotes: attenuated laser pulses, each containing 0.16 photons on average
after subtracting the total detection background at 7.12 KHz,
which includes the detector dark counts and the in-band noise photons created by the pump in the microdisk and ﬁbers
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own single-photon-level setup.
assertions.reader_inference: The input is attenuated coherent laser light at a mean of 0.16 photons per pulse, not a heralded single-photon source.

assertions.value: The authors report that without QZB the detection and gating rates are 59.20 KHz (62.88 KHz) and 465.0 KHz (395.0 KHz) on (off) resonance, yielding a photon probability of 0.112 (0.159) (±1.0%), which amounts to a 29.6% transmission loss at the resonance center.
quotes: the detection rate and the gating rate are 59.20 KHz (62.88 KHz) and 465.0 KHz (395.0 KHz), respectively, yielding a photon probability 0.112 (0.159) (±1.0%)
This amounts to a 29.6% transmission loss at the resonance center.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical measurement from one setup.
assertions.reader_inference: Reader arithmetic: (59.20 minus 7.12) divided by 465.0 is 0.112, so the on-resonance value has the 7.12 kHz background subtracted, while 62.88 divided by 395.0 is 0.159, which is the off-resonance value without subtraction. Subtracting the background from both would give about 0.141 off resonance and a loss near 21 percent, not 29.6 percent. The text may use another treatment that it does not state; this is a possible inconsistency in the text read.

assertions.value: The authors report a highest modulation extinction of 20.6±0.8% for single-photon-level signals, obtained when the signal wavelength is blue detuned by 0.01 nm from the resonance center, and state that this is consistent with their results using bright signal pulses.
quotes: The highest modulation extinction is 20.6±0.8% obtained when the signal wavelength is blue detuned by 0.01 nm from resonance center
which is consistent with our preceding results using bright signal pulses
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical result from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The 20.6 percent value is below the 48.2 percent and 51.0 percent bright-pulse values; the paper attributes the weaker QZB at the single-photon-level mode pair to poorer phase matching.

assertions.value: The authors tabulate, in the single-photon table, for three blue detunings listed in its first column, photon probabilities without QZB and with QZB of 0.112 and 0.118 (difference 0.006, extinction 12.7%), 0.123 and 0.133 (difference 0.010, extinction 20.6%), and 0.136 and 0.142 (difference 0.006, extinction 12.7%).
quotes: Detuning [nm] No QZB QZB ∆ Ext.
assertions.certainty_reason: An empirical table from one device in one study.
assertions.reader_inference: The text layer places the detuning values 0, 0.01 and 0.02 nm in the table's first column, as the row order and the text on the 0.01 nm best case indicate.

assertions.value: The authors state that, by using optimally phase-matched wavelengths for the signal and pump, they expect to improve the extinction by more than two folds with the current microdisk.
quotes: By using optimally phase-matched wavelengths for the signal and pump, we expect to improve the extinction by more than two folds with the current microdisk.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author expectation, not a measured result.
assertions.reader_inference: The bright-pulse results at the better phase-matched pair (48.2 and 51.0 percent) are about 2.3 to 2.5 times the 20.6 percent single-photon-level value, which is consistent with the stated expectation.

assertions.value: The authors describe fabricating the microdisk on LNOI, a 500 nm lithium-niobate thin film bonded on a 3 µm silicon dioxide layer, by etching 300 nm of film away with an inductively coupled plasma system to thin the film, electron-beam lithography with a negative resist, argon milling, and an undercut with buffered oxide etcher (6:1) to form the air-suspended structure.
quotes: which is a 500 nm lithium-niobate thin ﬁlm bonded on a 3 µm silicon dioxide layer above lithium niobate substrate
Thus, 300 nm LN thin ﬁlm is etched away using Oxford Plasmalab 100 Inductively Coupled Plasma (ICP) system.
BOE (buffered oxide etcher, 6:1) is used to undercut the microdisk to form the air-suspended structure.
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own fabrication procedure in the Methods.

assertions.value: The authors describe a locking-free method for stabilizing sum-frequency generation: mark the fundamental quasi-TE resonances with a broadband source, tune continuous-wave light to track the thermally shifted resonance using the brightness and mode distribution of the generated second-harmonic light, choose the best two modes, then switch to a quasi-continuous-wave signal and pulsed pump while retaining their wavelengths.
quotes: To achieve locking-free yet efﬁcient and stable SFG, we ﬁrstly use an OSA to measure the transmission of a broadband light from the ASE.
we could identify and choose the best two modes for sum frequency generation
we quickly switch to quasi-CW signal and pulsed pump while retaining their wavelengths
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state their own experimental procedure in the Methods.
assertions.reader_inference: The procedure compensates thermal drift by hand wavelength tuning; the paper does not report how long the stabilized state lasts.

assertions.value: The authors conclude that they have demonstrated quantum Zeno blockade on chip, where a light is modulated by another without them overlapping in the cavity in the asymptotic limit, and that this interaction-free implementation overcomes several fundamental difficulties of quantum nonlinear optics such as phase distortion, Raman scattering and pulse distortion.
quotes: we have demonstrated quantum Zeno blockade on chip, where a light is modulated by another without them overlapping in the cavity in the asymptotic limit
This distinct ”interaction-free” implementation overcomes several fundamental difﬁculties with quantum nonlinear optics, such as phase distortion, Raman scattering, and pulse distortion
assertions.certainty_reason: An author conclusion; the reported measurements are modulation extinctions and a photon noise level, not a direct test of the absence of interaction.
assertions.reader_inference: The text read reports transmitted signal depletion and noise counts. It reports no separate measurement of the generated sum-frequency light during the QZB runs, and no phase-distortion or pulse-distortion measurement, so the 'interaction-free' and 'overcomes' statements rest on the authors' interpretation and earlier theory.

assertions.value: The authors state that they show single photons can be modulated with low excessive noise.
quotes: we show that single photons can be modulated with low excessive noise
assertions.certainty_reason: An author conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: The input was attenuated laser pulses at a mean of 0.16 photons per pulse, and the reported noise probability of 9.3 × 10−2 per pump pulse is reduced to 7.2 × 10−3 per mode only under assumed single-mode detection.

assertions.value: The authors state that the next step is to improve the phase matching while replacing the current fiber taper with a waveguide coupler, so that all-optical operations can be achieved at low error rate and cascaded on a single chip.
quotes: The next step is to improve the phase matching while replacing the current ﬁber taper with a waveguide coupler
all-optical operations can be achieved at low error rate while cascaded on a single chip
assertions.certainty_reason: The authors state the open problems of the current device in the conclusion.
assertions.reader_inference: The current device depends on a fiber taper coupler and imperfect phase matching, so it is not yet an integrated on-chip circuit element.

assertions.value: The authors state that further increasing the cavity quality factor can lead to strong photon-photon interaction for interaction-free quantum logic gates with high fidelity.
quotes: Further increasing the cavity quality factor can lead to strong photon photon interaction for ”interaction-free” quantum logic gates with high ﬁdelity.
assertions.certainty_reason: An author expectation, not a result of this paper.
assertions.reader_inference: The loaded quality factor reported here is 2.6 × 104; no photon-photon interaction or logic gate is demonstrated.
